chain.label: DC-8 maintenance documents lacked securing-hardware detail and a discrete post-rigging inspection item
chain.trigger: this section of the Emery DC-8 MM did not contain a list of (or other guidance specifically detailing) the required hardware for the proper installation and security of the control tab crank fitting/pushrod attachment or detailed steps regarding the inspection of this attachment

chain.label: Control tab linkage design permits a disconnected pushrod to escape the crank lugs and jam the tab
chain.trigger: the current DC-8 design does not preclude a catastrophic result from a disconnection or failure of the existing control tab crank fitting to pushrod attachment

chain.label: Right elevator control tab pushrod attachment bolt not properly secured or inspected
chain.trigger: The disconnection was caused by the failure to properly secure and inspect the attachment bolt.

caused_by.evidence: there was no discrete work card step requiring an inspector to re-verify the security of attachments after the rigging work was completed

chain.label: Unsecured attachment bolt free to migrate, concealed behind the inboard control tab fairing
chain.trigger: the bolt must have separated because it had not been properly secured; that is, the required castellated nut was either never installed, or it was improperly installed (for example, installed without a cotter pin)

caused_by.evidence: the bolt attaching the accident airplane's right elevator control tab was improperly secured and inspected, either during the most recent D inspection or subsequent maintenance

chain.label: Right elevator control tab disconnected from its pushrod and restricted at extreme trailing-edge-down deflection
chain.trigger: the bolt connecting the right elevator control tab crank fitting to the pushrod migrated out of the fitting, allowing the control tab to disengage from its pushrod and shift to a TED position

caused_by.evidence: The bolt and associated hardware that normally secures the right elevator control tab pushrod to the tab crank fitting was missing and not recovered.
the TED [control] tab motion and the subsequent [push]rod end escape from between the crank [fitting] lugs was a mode that had not been anticipated

chain.label: Crew did not recognize the abnormal elevator indication during the taxi and 80-knot elevator checks and continued the takeoff
chain.trigger: The flight crew appeared satisfied with the results of the 80-knot elevator check and continued the takeoff roll.

caused_by.evidence: the EPI needle would not have moved below the neutral mark during the 80-knot elevator check, thus providing an indication that the elevator was not fully operational

chain.label: Uncommanded nose-up pitch at rotation as both elevators were driven trailing edge up
chain.trigger: the airplane pitched from 0.2º ANU about 1949:02 to 5.3º ANU at 1949:08; the pitch continued to increase despite the forward movement of the control column

caused_by.evidence: the aerodynamic forces acting on the extreme TED-deflected right control tab would have driven both elevator surfaces abnormally TEU, resulting in a strong airplane nose-up elevator effect
The captain must know the elevator is working properly early in the takeoff roll. If he is in doubt, he should consider aborting the takeoff.

chain.label: Loss of pitch control; crew unable to counter the nose-up moment while maneuvering to return
chain.trigger: despite the large nose-down forces the pilots applied to the control columns, the pilots were unable to overcome the effects of the restricted right elevator control tab

caused_by.evidence: the airplane rolled and pitched and climbed and descended, as the pilots tried different combinations of flight control inputs and engine power settings to counter the airplane's uncommanded pitch-up

chain.label: Impact with an automobile salvage yard about 1 mile east of the departure runway
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted the ground in a left-wing-low, slightly nose-up attitude in an automobile salvage yard, about 1 mile east of the departure runway.

caused_by.evidence: probable cause of the accident was a loss of pitch control resulting from the disconnection of the right elevator control tab

chain.label: Three flight crewmembers killed; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The three flight crewmembers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed.

caused_by.evidence: the captain and flight engineer died as a result of thermal and traumatic injuries, and the first officer died of thermal injuries and inhalation of combustion products
